name: Tennessee

statute.readVia: Not read on an official text: the official code is the LexisNexis portal (not readable by script) and tn.gov refused our connection. Figures come from a non-official copy of the 2023 code archived on 2024-12-11. Public Chapter 602 of 2024 (official, publications.tnsosfiles.com/acts/113/pub/pc0602.pdf) only rewords the officer exemption.

windshield.strip: no material reducing windshield transmittance below 70%, except the manufacturer's standard installed shade band

frontSide.note: aftermarket material may not have visible light transmittance below 35%; front door windows are never exempt

backSide.note: exempt where federal regulations allow the model to have those windows darker (e.g. factory privacy glass on MPVs/trucks) - 55-9-107(a)(6)(A)(i); interpretation of whether aftermarket film is covered not settled by the text

tint.measuredHow: the material itself ('any material that has a visible light transmittance of less than thirty-five percent'); field comparison test by officers per Safety Commissioner procedure
tint.certificateOrSticker: Professional installers must affix a label on the lower right corner of the driver's window (business name + 'Complies with Tennessee Code Annotated, § 55-9-107') and give a signed receipt to keep with registration documents; owner bears burden of proof of compliance

medicalExemption.text: Physician's statement to the Commissioner of Safety; Department's medical review board recommends the exemption and degree of tint; the Commissioner issues a certificate or decal to display in the vehicle; appeal under the UAPA

penalty.text: Class C misdemeanor (also for refusing a field comparison test); officers may stop a vehicle on reasonable belief of a violation

tint.lastAmended: 2024 (Public Chapter 602, SB 1864: "full-time, salaried police officer" replaced by "POST-certified law enforcement officer"; percentages not touched)
quotes: (A) Has a visible light transmittance of less than thirty-five percent (35%); or (B) With the exception of the manufacturer's standard installed shade band, reduces the visible light transmittance in the windshield below seventy percent (70%).
This subdivision (a)(6) shall not be construed in any way to exempt the front door windows of any motor vehicle of any kind from the specifications of subdivision (a)(1)(A).
It is a Class C misdemeanor for the operator of a motor vehicle to refuse to submit to the field comparison test ... or for any person to otherwise violate any provisions of this section.

radarDetector.note: No state ban found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

read.noteEn: The official Tennessee Code (published by LexisNexis) could not be read, so these figures are not confirmed on an official text. They come from a non-official copy of the 2023 code, archived on December 11, 2024. The only later change found on an official site, Public Chapter 602 of 2024, rewords the officer exemption and leaves the percentages as they were.
read.noteEs: No se pudo leer el Código oficial de Tennessee (publicado por LexisNexis), así que estas cifras no están confirmadas en un texto oficial. Vienen de una copia no oficial del código de 2023, archivada el 11 de diciembre de 2024. El único cambio posterior hallado en un sitio oficial, el Public Chapter 602 de 2024, reformula la exención de los agentes y no toca los porcentajes.
